scope: Bounded RFC 3501 LIST response support: line-bound mailbox literals, hierarchy delimiters, strict modified UTF-7 validation, exact remote wire identity, and \Noselect fences. This is source and loopback evidence only. It is separate from the MIME full-fetch endpoint seam and does not update MSR requirement status.

source.sourceTreeStatus: The native input digest is recorded for provenance only. This mutable source checkout has subsequent scoped changes and is not asserted to match that digest.

rfc3501.hierarchyDelimiter: Accepted only as NIL or one quoted character. Atom, literal, and multi-character delimiters are rejected because they are not valid RFC 3501 LIST delimiter grammar.
rfc3501.mailboxName: Accepted as atom, quoted string, or a literal bound to the originating LIST response line. Accepted non-ASCII names must be canonical modified UTF-7.

implementation.literalBinding: ImapLiteralItem::ListResponse stores the originating response-line index. LIST parsing consumes only literals whose index matches its LIST line; FETCH literals and extra literals cannot provide a mailbox name.

resourceLimit.aggregateListLiteralBytes: 8192 multiplied by the existing maximum response-literal count
resourceLimit.enforcement: The declared literal length is rejected by the command reader before mailbox-byte allocation.

implementation.remoteIdentity: The accepted remote mailbox name stays as its exact canonical wire string in mailbox catalog state. Logical configured names are encoded through the strict modified UTF-7 codec only for matching.

noSelect.attributeMatching: Case-insensitive canonical comparison of LIST attributes. Unknown attributes, including \HasChildren, are retained only as response metadata and do not alter selectability; a co-present \Noselect still fences the mailbox.
noSelect.specialUse: A \Noselect special-use listing is ignored. A successful LIST with no selectable special-use candidate retains the configured fallback.
noSelect.knownTarget: An exact configured mailbox that LIST marks \Noselect fails before SELECT, APPEND, MOVE, or delete mutation commands.
noSelect.pruning: Malformed or noncanonical LIST literals fail synchronization before catalog replacement, preserving the existing local mailbox family.

implementation.failureHandling: LIST parse and transport errors now propagate to synchronization, search, Sent-copy save, and mutation paths. They no longer become an empty listing that could permit a configured fallback action.

focusedVerification.productionBoundary: The seven LIST tests include a fragmented public-TLS loopback connection through the production IMAP connector, exact LIST then SELECT transcript checks, Store reopen verification, selectable unknown-attribute tolerance, and no-command assertions after rejected LIST data or co-present unknown attribute plus \Noselect.
sensitivity: scripted_reset_noncanonical_list_literal_cannot_select_or_prune_a_family supplies the formerly accepted literal form with noncanonical modified UTF-7. The test now proves no SELECT occurs and the existing Sent::Legacy family remains present.

malformed_list_after_known_noselect_sent_mailbox_never_reaches_append supplies a valid \NoSelect \Sent line followed by a malformed line. It proves the malformed LIST failure is not treated as an empty listing and APPEND is never issued.
known_noselect_source_never_reaches_select_or_move and known_noselect_source_never_reaches_select_or_delete assert no SELECT or destructive protocol command follows the fenced source.

list_literal_parser_rejects_missing_extra_noncanonical_and_nonselect_targets proves unknown attributes and \HasChildren do not make a selectable mailbox non-selectable, while an unknown attribute cannot hide a co-present case-mixed \Noselect. The production TLS sync transcript includes an unknown attribute and still selects the exact wire identity.

findings: High: LIST failures were being converted to empty listings in paths including Sent-copy saving, allowing fallback actions after malformed server data.
Medium: permanent delete checked UIDPLUS before LIST and could SELECT a known \Noselect source.
Low: delimiter parsing admitted forms outside RFC 3501 grammar.
initialIndependentSecurityReview.remediation: All LIST consumers propagate parse failures; delete lists and fences after UIDPLUS validation; delimiter parsing accepts only NIL or one quoted character.

finalIndependentReview.scope: LIST implementation and the separate full-fetch endpoint seam
finalIndependentReview.finalCorrection: Delimiter parsing no longer delegates to the generic astring parser. It accepts NIL or exactly one printable seven-bit quoted byte, permits escaping only quote or backslash, and rejects raw quote, raw backslash, control, raw Unicode, invalid escape, atom, literal, and multi-character forms.

separateMimeFullFetchEndpointSeam.status: implemented separately from LIST; dependent MIME tests are owned and executed by the MIME workstream
separateMimeFullFetchEndpointSeam.productionPath: fetch_full_message passes no endpoint override into its private common implementation, retaining normal production certificate-verifying connection selection.
separateMimeFullFetchEndpointSeam.testPath: A cfg(test) loopback endpoint helper delegates into that same private implementation.

remainingLimits: MSR-3501-list remains unmarked in machine-readable standards metadata until the governed source3 finalization and final independent review complete.
This evidence does not claim full RFC 3501 conformance, independent-server integration, provider acceptance, native app verification, or a full source suite.
Literal hierarchy delimiters are rejected by design because RFC 3501 defines the hierarchy delimiter as NIL or a quoted character.
